test.title: login API returns a token
test.error:
Error: expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality
Expected: 200
Received: 423

triage.reason: The API returned 423 Locked, which is an intentional account-lockout response, not a malformed or broken endpoint — the service is behaving as designed. The test posts `password: 'pass123'` for customer3@practicesoftwaretesting.com, which is not the seeded credential for this demo API (customer accounts use welcome01), so the login fails and repeated runs lock the account, yielding a deterministic 423 on all 3 attempts. Fixing the test data (and unlocking/rotating the account) is the action, not an app fix. The alternative explanation is shared state — another test or earlier run locked the same account, which would make this flaky — but the non-standard password in the test and the identical failure on every retry point at the test data first.
triage.evidence: "Expected: 200 / Received: 423" at `expect(response.status()).toBe(200);`, with the request body `data: { email: 'customer3@practicesoftwaretesting.com', password: 'pass123' }`. Status 423 Locked = account lockout after failed login attempts, and the test "failed on every attempt (3 attempts)".
triage.next_step: POST to https://api.practicesoftwaretesting.com/users/login manually with customer@practicesoftwaretesting.com / welcome01 (a known-good seeded credential) to confirm the endpoint returns 200 and an access_token; if it does, correct the email/password in tests/api.spec.ts:5 to valid seeded credentials (ideally from an env var or fixture) and use a dedicated account that other tests don't lock.

triage.reason: The mock never intercepted the product request, so the empty-state message could not appear. The route glob `'**/products'` does not match the real request, which carries a query string (Playwright glob matching includes the query), e.g. `/products?between=price,1,100&page=0`. Evidence that interception failed: the failure-time accessibility tree shows nine live products and 3 pages of pagination instead of an empty list. The assertion's precondition was never set up, so this is a test-side defect, not app misbehaviour; identical failure on all 3 attempts also excludes flakiness.
triage.evidence: Test code: `await page.route('**/products', (route) => route.fulfill({ status: 200, json: { data: [] } }));` vs. page state at failure: `link "ECO Combination Pliers CO₂: A B C D E $14.15"` and `navigation "Pagination"` → `listitem: You're on page 1`, `listitem: page 2`, `listitem: page 3`. Error: `element(s) not found` for `getByText('There are no products found.')`.
triage.next_step: Change the route pattern to also match query strings — e.g. `await page.route(/\/products(\?|$)/, ...)` or `page.route('**/products?*', ...)` — then re-run and confirm from the network log that the request was fulfilled; while there, verify the actual empty-state copy in the app's product-list component matches 'There are no products found.'

triage.reason: The test blocks on a response predicate that no request in this app can satisfy: it demands an HTTP method of 'QUERY' and a URL ending exactly in '/products' (which also excludes the filter query string). The accessibility tree proves the feature itself worked — the Pliers checkbox is checked and the list is reduced to the Pliers products — so the app responded correctly while the test waited forever on an impossible network match. Deterministic failure across all 3 attempts fits a wrong predicate, not timing.
triage.evidence: Error: "page.waitForResponse: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded." at the predicate `(response) => response.request().method() === 'QUERY' && response.url().endsWith('/products')`, while the page shows `checkbox "Pliers" [checked] [active] [ref=e83]` and only `heading "Combination Pliers"` / `link "ECO Pliers ..."` in the results.
triage.next_step: Open DevTools Network (or run with `PWDEBUG=1`/a `page.on('request')` log) while checking the Pliers filter to capture the real method and URL, then change the predicate to something like `response.request().method() === 'GET' && response.url().includes('/products')`.

triage.reason: The timeout is not the app failing to react — the accessibility tree captured at failure shows the "Pliers" checkbox as [checked] and the product grid already showing pliers products ("Combination Pliers", "Pliers"), so the filter request/response round-trip clearly happened and rendered. What never matched is the test's own response predicate: it demands an HTTP method of 'QUERY' and a URL that ends exactly in '/products'. The Toolshop app issues a normal GET to /products with query-string parameters (e.g. ?by_category=...), so neither condition can ever be true and page.waitForResponse simply hangs until the 30s test timeout. Failing identically on all 3 attempts (deterministic, no timing variance) also argues against flakiness, and the hint "timeout" is only a symptom of the bad matcher. The fix belongs in the test, not the app.
triage.evidence: Predicate in the spec: `response.request().method() === 'QUERY' && response.url().endsWith('/products')`, failing at `const categoryResponse = page.waitForResponse(isProductsQuery);` with "Error: page.waitForResponse: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded." — while the page state shows `checkbox "Pliers" [checked] [active] [ref=e83]` and `heading "Combination Pliers"`, i.e. the filter did apply.
triage.next_step: Re-run the test with `page.on('request', r => console.log(r.method(), r.url()))` (or open DevTools Network while checking the "Pliers" filter) to capture the real filter call, then relax the predicate to match it — most likely `response.request().method() === 'GET' && response.url().includes('/products')`.

Identical failure on all 3 attempts rules out flakiness, and the surrounding seeded defects ("Contakt", "Reltded products", Home link pointing to #/contact) indicate this build has intentional UI bugs. Residual doubt only because a silently renamed toast string would look similar.
triage.evidence: Error line: "Locator: getByText('Product added to shopping cart.') Expected: visible ... Error: element(s) not found", while the same snapshot shows the add succeeded: - menuitem "cart": - link "cart": - /url: "#/checkout" - text:  1
triage.next_step: Manually add "Combination Pliers" to the cart on the product page and watch for the confirmation toast; if none renders while the cart badge increments, file it as a missing-confirmation bug (check the DOM/network for the toast component rather than changing the locator).
